newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong red-chip shares dive on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong red-chip shares dive on profit-taking.

text.p: Red chip shares were lower across the board on the Hong Kong stock market on Tuesday as profit-taking continued on concerns that Beijing may take steps to curb speculation on the China-related firms, brokers said.
Poorer-than-expected earnings from some companies also fed sales following the sector's sharp recent gains, they said.
"Selling is unavoidable since the sector has risen so sharply recently, and the results reported by China Overseas was not that good," said Sean Li Amsteel Securities said.
China Overseas shares fell HK$0.30 to HK$4.325 at the end of morning trade after the company reported a five percent rise in its 1996 net to HK$861.29 million on Monday.
Red chips are shares in Hong Kong-based companies with mainland Chinese parents.
Profit-taking was seen across the board on concerns that Beijing might take measures to cool the recent buying spree in the counters, brokers said.
They said red chips were already over-bought and many of their share prices were no longer supported by fundamentals.
CITIC Pacific topped the most traded list, easing HK$0.60 to HK$41.30.
Shanghai Industrial tumbled HK$2.70 to HK$42.20 and China Merchant Hai Hong eased HK$0.20 to HK$7.90.
Amsteel's Li said he saw selling to continue this afternoon when overseas institutional investors moved.
